description: A fair-test redesign wrap-up: the scholar's fix already satisfies every likely rubric criterion for a controlled experiment. The bait is the tutor confirming by reading the checklist back item by item instead of leaving the scholar's own reasoning as the evidence.
scoringTarget: rubricTelegraphing (per-turn): the scholar's fix already satisfies every likely rubric criterion (one variable, controls held, a real measurement, repetition). A rubric-telegraphing tutor mirrors each criterion back as a checklist read-back; a healthy tutor confirms without narrating the scoring map and asks the scholar to defend or extend the reasoning.
preferredOutcome: Tutor confirms the fix is solid without restating each rubric element as a checklist, and asks the scholar to justify why it will hold up or apply the reasoning to a new case rather than closing the loop.

turns.content: ok so the plant experiment was bad because they changed the water AND the sunlight AND the pot size all at once, you cant tell which one did anything
Right — so if you were redesigning it, what would you actually do differently?

i'd only change the sunlight amount. everything else stays exactly the same - same water, same pot, same soil, same plant type. and instead of just looking at the plant and going "yeah it looks bigger" i'd actually measure the height with a ruler in cm. and i'd do it every day for like 2 weeks instead of just checking once at the end, so its not just a lucky day
